---
title: "Learning Roadmap"
---

The default pace is approximately **10–12 hours per week**. The first nine stages form a roughly two-year core; Stage 10 is a research specialisation phase.

| Stage | Subject | Indicative duration | Main output |
|---|---|---:|---|
| 1 | Research computing | 10 weeks | Reproducible research repository |
| Bridge | Machine Learning Foundations |
| 2 | Statistical learning | 10 weeks | Prediction benchmark project |
| 3 | Modern causal ML | 12 weeks | Causal ML replication/project |
| 4 | Deep learning | 12 weeks | Transformer components from scratch |
| 5 | Optimisation & algorithms | 12 weeks | Algorithmic allocation project |
| 6 | Bandits & RL | 14 weeks | Dynamic pricing/RL project |
| 7 | Algorithmic game theory | 14 weeks | Computational mechanism project |
| 8 | Multi-agent learning | 10 weeks | Artificial-market experiment |
| 9 | Structured/relational FMs | 12 weeks | Relational ML benchmark |
| 10 | Research specialisation | 6–12 months | Working-paper-level project |

## Parallel mathematics spine

Run alongside the main sequence:

- **Months 1–6:** linear algebra, probability, multivariate calculus, likelihood and asymptotics.
- **Months 6–12:** convexity, duality, KKT conditions, concentration and high-dimensional statistics.
- **Months 12–24:** Markov processes, dynamic programming, regret analysis, fixed points and complexity.

## Research-output ladder

1. Reproducible repositories
2. Replication studies
3. Algorithms implemented from papers
4. Frontier-paper reproductions
5. Research extensions
